searchText: EIP-3455 raised a few security concerns but I'm back with an audited solution to user regret on Ethereum. https://github.com/ethereum/EIPs/pull/6810 The question would then be for factory contract deployments or for data usage within the contract itself? If it's storing deployed code then that is a non-starter since we aim to remove bytecode observability. We could make generic deployment factories that _must_ be delegatecalled and would deploy their contract with suitable auxdata to address that. If it's to re-use data across multiple contracts (or a cluster of the same dapp to avoid the 24Kib rule) then perhaps we use that as motivation to re-examine size limits. Note EOF has a built in 64KiB function limit, but can do up to 1024 functions within a container. Data similarly has a 64KiB limit. This is based on the two byte size value. Unfortunately I really don't recall Nick's argument.
